item.title: Built in 1966, San Francisco's Empress of China closed in 2016; 10 years later it reopened its doors
item.description: The iconic Empress of China building in San Francisco has achieved community ownership after a decade-long effort. A coalition of six Asian American non-profits came together to acquire this historic site, aiming to convert it into a thriving arts and cultural campus. The restoration project aligns with broader economic and cultural revitalization goals, inviting future public sessions to influence its architectural evolution.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: In 2015, Hawaii rescued fragments of a coral found only in Kaneohe Bay; after its wild colonies...
item.description: Marine biologists rescued rare Hawaiian coral fragments from Kaneohe Bay in 2015. These fragments were grown into mature colonies using a land-based nursery method. The grown corals were then returned to their natural habitat in Kaneohe Bay. Field checks confirmed the reintroduced corals successfully adjusted to their surroundings. This project demonstrates the effectiveness of coral arks for preventing species extinction.

item.title: In 2021, a developer bought an empty Park City lot for $6 million; 4 years of construction later...
item.description: A Park City mountain land bought for six million dollars became a thirty-seven million dollar luxury home. This sale set the highest residential price ever recorded within the city limits. The seventeen thousand square foot mansion was completed after four years of construction. It features extensive ski-in, ski-out facilities and high-end amenities for wealthy buyers. Limited supply and high demand continue to boost Utah mountain luxury housing markets.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: Mecca Pact, but no troops yet: Pak expresses 'solidarity' with Saudi after Houthi attacks
item.description: Pakistan voiced strong solidarity with Saudi Arabia following recent Houthi attacks. These strikes threaten regional peace and could disrupt global energy supplies. Prime Minister Sharif discussed these issues with Crown Prince Mohammed bin Salman. The recent Houthi advances have also intensified concerns over Red Sea shipping routes. A mutual-defense pact between Pakistan, Saudi Arabia, and Turkiye is now under renewed focus.
item.dc:creator: Yashasvi Vasistha

item.title: How Monty Don turned a 2-acre field into a garden millions love
item.description: Monty Don is stepping down from Gardeners' World after 23 years. He transformed his private garden, Longmeadow, into a nationally recognized space. Viewers watched his garden evolve over three decades of television. Don learned to observe his land before making any changes. Gardening provides a sense of purpose, freedom, and empowerment for people.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: 28 Tasmanian devils were moved to an island; 3,000 penguin pairs later disappeared
item.description: In 2012, 28 Tasmanian devils were introduced to Maria Island as an insurance population against facial tumour disease. The devils thrived, reaching up to 90, but experts say their presence came at a heavy cost to local wildlife. A survey later found Maria Island’s little penguin colonies had disappeared, wiping out an estimated 3,000 breeding pairs.
item.dc:creator: TOI Science Desk

item.title: Dubbo Wastewater Plant Starts: New catalyst breaks down stubborn pollutants; city bets on recycled water
item.description: This week, an innovative wastewater treatment facility was inaugurated in Dubbo, New South Wales, marking a significant upgrade in regional water management. Capable of processing large quantities of wastewater each year, the plant employs cutting-edge technology to effectively decompose challenging contaminants. The recycled water generated will have diverse applications, aiding local communities, especially in drought-affected areas, by transforming wastewater into a crucial resource.

item.title: 90-year-old iconic Twin Chimneys motel in Cheyenne torn down for a coffee drive-thru
item.description: The Twin Chimneys Motor Court in Cheyenne, Wyoming, was demolished this week after almost 90 years. Its distinctive twin stone chimneys, a landmark along the historic Lincoln Highway, fell in about 30 seconds. The site will now make way for a 7 Brew Coffee drive-thru stand, ending the story of the once-popular motor court.

item.title: In 1876, Los Angeles built the Perry House; 99 years later it was moved to Heritage Square
item.description: Los Angeles' historic Perry Mansion celebrated its 150th anniversary by opening its second floor. This rare access allowed visitors to see preserved 19th-century rooms and raise funds. The grand Victorian residence was built in 1876 for businessman William Hayes Perry. Preservationists saved the mansion from demolition in 1975 and moved it to Heritage Square Museum. Funds raised will support ongoing structural conservation and protection of the historic wooden building.

item.title: Canada explores ‘associate member’ status with EU amid US trade tensions
item.description: Canada explores becoming an associate member of the European Union. Prime Minister Mark Carney seeks stronger economic and strategic ties with the bloc. This move comes as Canada's trade relationship with the United States has worsened. Discussions focus on free movement of goods, services, and workers. Deeper cooperation is also being considered in energy and technology sectors.
